name: National Mars ambitions
operator: MBRSC and the UAE Space Agency; KASA (South Korea); others
short_status: Two national targets with no Mars hardware behind them: the UAE's Mars 2117 settlement programme of 14 February 2017 and South Korea's 2045 robotic landing goal, set 28 November 2022. Both stood on 24 August 2026.
tagline: MBRSC and the UAE Space Agency; KASA (South Korea); others · Multinational · Programme · 2017 · Announced Planned
stats: UAE target year for a first human settlement on Mars, set on 14 February 2017
Korean target year for a Mars landing, set on 28 November 2022
KASA's entire 2026 exploration budget line, against 100 trillion won promised by 2045

facts.label: The Mars 2117 announcement
facts.value: Unveiled on Tuesday 14 February 2017 in Dubai, on the sidelines of the fifth World Government Summit, by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, and Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, then Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi. The Emirates News Agency described a project which "aims at its final stage to establish the first inhabitable human settlement in Mars by 2117".

facts.label: What was promised, in their words
facts.value: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid: "The new project is a seed that we plant today, and we expect future generations to reap the benefits, driven by its passion to learn to unveil a new knowledge." Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, on the same day: "The Mars 2117 Project is a long term project, where our first objective is to develop our educational system so our sons will be able to lead scientific research across the various sectors." The first phase was described as preparing human cadres rather than building spacecraft.

facts.label: Who runs it
facts.value: On 22 February 2017, eight days after the unveiling, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid directed the Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre to lead Mars 2117 and prepare a hundred-year plan. The centre was told to focus on preparing specialised national cadres in space science, research, artificial intelligence, robotics and advanced space technologies, to produce a detailed five-year plan covering technological, logistical and technical aspects, and to run a parallel media plan at local, regional and international level.

facts.label: The four pillars
facts.value: MBRSC's own Mars 2117 page organises the programme as Research and Development, Enablement, Education and Collaboration. Its stated mission is "To prepare cadres of space scientists and engineers that can enable the UAE to contribute to the development of space travel and planetary settlement capabilities, in particular the establishment of a human colony on the Red Planet". Its stated objectives are life support systems for human settlements on other planets alongside research addressing food, water and energy security on Earth. No spacecraft, launch or landing is named anywhere on the page.

facts.label: Mars Science City
facts.value: Announced on Tuesday 26 September 2017 at the UAE government annual meetings in Abu Dhabi. As described that day, in the future tense of a project being launched rather than opened: AED 500 million, 1.9 million square feet, several domes, laboratories for food, energy and water, a museum whose walls would be 3D printed from Emirati desert sand, and a plan for a team to live inside the simulated city for one year. WAM called it the largest space simulation city ever built. The design team was led by MBRSC and Dubai Municipality with the architects Bjarke Ingels.

facts.label: Where Mars Science City stands
facts.value: Unclear, and that is the honest answer. The UAE government portal still carries the 2017 description and the 2017 figures on a page last updated 30 December 2024, in the future tense: "the UAE will build a complex of buildings called Mars Science City". MBRSC's current Missions and Projects page lists the astronaut programme, satellites, the Rashid rover and the Emirates Airlock, and does not list Mars 2117 or Mars Science City at all. We found no official announcement of construction start, completion or opening.

facts.label: What the UAE has actually done
facts.value: The concrete Emirati record at Mars is one orbiter. The Emirates Mars Mission probe Hope launched from Tanegashima on 20 July 2020 and reached Mars orbit in February 2021, and has its own entry in this catalogue. The country's other approved deep space project, the Emirati interplanetary mission planned for 2028, goes to the asteroid belt. Mars is not its destination. The Rashid rover went to the Moon and the Emirates Airlock is for lunar Gateway.

facts.label: The analogue programme
facts.value: The most substantive Mars-directed Emirati activity is human research. Under the UAE Analog Programme, Emirati crew member Obaid AlSuwaidi spent 45 days from 1 November to 16 December 2024 inside NASA's Human Exploration Research Analog at Johnson Space Center, as part of HERA Campaign 7 Mission 4, with communication delays of up to five minutes and a virtual reality Mars walk. The study ran 18 human health experiments, six of them led by MBRSC with UAEU, Mohammed Bin Rashid University of Medicine and Health Sciences and the American University of Sharjah. MBRSC also co-ran the eight-month SIRIUS-21 isolation study in Moscow from 4 November 2021 to 3 July 2022.

facts.label: The Korean announcement
facts.value: On 28 November 2022 President Yoon Suk-yeol said South Korea would land a robotic spacecraft on the Moon in 2032 and on Mars in 2045, the centenary of liberation from Japanese colonial rule. "By 2045, we will be able to plant our national flag on Mars," he said in a keynote at the Korea Space Forum 2022 in Seoul. He promised to double the government space budget within five years and to funnel at least 100 trillion won, then about 74.7 billion dollars, into the space sector by 2045. South Korea's space budget for 2022 was 734 billion won.

facts.label: It is a robotic target
facts.value: The 2045 goal as announced is an uncrewed robotic landing, and Mars was a new objective for South Korea at the time; the Moon date had also slipped, from 2030 under the previous administration to 2032. Details were expected in the fourth revision of the Basic Plan for Promotion of Space Development, the five-year plan running to 2027.

facts.label: The agency that followed
facts.value: The Korea AeroSpace Administration (우주항공청, KASA) opened on 27 May 2024, under a special act on its establishment and operation enacted on 26 January 2024 and taking effect on 27 May. It is based in Sacheon, South Gyeongsang province, and it is the first single Korean agency to hold the state space programmes that were previously spread across several ministries.

facts.label: How KASA states the goal now
facts.value: KASA's vision page sets the target as becoming one of the five leading aerospace nations, with a government budget of 1.5 trillion won by 2027 and national investment of 100 trillion won by 2045. Under exploration it gives the line 달을 넘어 화성·심우주로 탐사 확대, expand exploration beyond the Moon to Mars and deep space, with sub-items covering an exploration roadmap, lunar science, extending Korea's horizon into deep space, asteroid mining and preparing a crewed space programme. No Mars date appears on the page.

facts.label: The 2025 roadmap
facts.value: On 4 September 2025 KASA announced that its sixth Space Development Promotion Working Committee, held in writing from 28 August to 4 September, had approved the 대한민국 우주탐사 로드맵, the Korea Space Exploration Roadmap, containing mid and long-term goals and implementation plans to 2045. Its stated vision is expanding human knowledge and expanding the territory of the space economy, and its core goals include use of space resources and 달·화성 기지건설, Moon and Mars base construction. The roadmap covers low Earth orbit microgravity, lunar exploration, solar and space science, planetary exploration and astrophysics. This press release is the fullest account of the roadmap we could read; we could not open the roadmap document itself, and we found no confirmation of when or whether it was published in full.

facts.label: What Korea actually spends
facts.value: KASA's 2026 budget was fixed at 1.1201 trillion won by a National Assembly plenary vote on 2 December 2025, up 155.2 billion won or 16.1 per cent on 2025's 964.9 billion won, and the first time the agency has passed one trillion won. Of that, 96.8 billion won goes to the exploration line, described as creating future space livelihoods through challenging exploration. The other five lines are transportation, satellites, aviation, industrial ecosystem and workforce. Against a stated 100 trillion won of national investment by 2045, this is the actual annual figure.

facts.label: The other national visions
facts.value: India's Space Vision 2047, as ISRO chairman S. Somanath set it out in the Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture in New Delhi on 26 October 2024, centres on an Indian landing on the Moon and on the Bharatiya Antariksh space station as a launching point for lunar exploration. In the Press Information Bureau's account of that lecture, Mars appears only as a destination already visited, on the way to future missions to Venus. No Indian Mars date, crewed or robotic, has been announced. China has published far more than either the UAE or Korea and is covered in its own entry in this catalogue.

facts.label: Why we file these as visions
facts.value: None of them has the three things a mission needs: an approved project, a funded vehicle and a committed date attached to that vehicle. The UAE's target is a century away and is described by its own operators as an education and research programme. Korea's is twenty years away and has been restated in the 2025 roadmap as base construction rather than a landing. Both are policy commitments to a direction. That is a real thing, and it is not the same thing as a spacecraft.

timeline: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum and Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan unveil the Mars 2117 Project at the fifth World Government Summit in Dubai, with the stated final-stage aim of the first inhabitable human settlement on Mars by 2117.

Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid directs the Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre to lead the project and prepare a hundred-year plan, focused on national cadres in space science, research, artificial intelligence, robotics and advanced space technologies, plus a detailed five-year plan and a media plan.

Mars Science City is launched at the UAE government annual meetings in Abu Dhabi: AED 500 million, 1.9 million square feet, several domes, a year-long crewed simulation and a museum with 3D printed walls made from Emirati desert sand, designed with Bjarke Ingels.
The Emirates Mars Mission orbiter Hope launches from Tanegashima, the concrete Emirati result at Mars and a separate mission from the 2117 programme.
MBRSC co-runs the eight-month SIRIUS-21 isolation study in Moscow with Roscosmos and NASA, its first long-duration analogue involvement.

President Yoon Suk-yeol tells the Korea Space Forum in Seoul that South Korea will land a robotic spacecraft on the Moon in 2032 and on Mars in 2045, and promises at least 100 trillion won into the space sector by 2045.
The Korea AeroSpace Administration opens in Sacheon, under a special act enacted on 26 January 2024.

Emirati crew member Obaid AlSuwaidi spends 45 days inside NASA's HERA habitat at Johnson Space Center as part of Campaign 7 Mission 4, running 18 human health experiments with five-minute communication delays.
KASA issues 대한민국 우주과학탐사 추진전략, its space science exploration strategy, at the third National Space Committee. This is the document the 2045 exploration roadmap is later built on.
KASA announces that its sixth Space Development Promotion Working Committee has approved the Korea Space Exploration Roadmap to 2045, whose core goals include Moon and Mars base construction.
The National Assembly fixes KASA's 2026 budget at 1.1201 trillion won, the agency's first year above one trillion, of which 96.8 billion won is the exploration line.

Both targets still stand in official material. The UAE government portal's Mars Science City page, last updated 30 December 2024, still describes the city in the future tense, and MBRSC's current projects page does not list Mars 2117. KASA's vision page carries Mars as a direction without a date.

images.caption: BIG's aerial visualisation of Mars Science City as it would sit in the desert outside Dubai, five geodesic domes clustered on a green plot beside a looping access road, with a highway at the left and a hazy sunrise behind.
BIG's visualisation of the same domes transposed onto Mars, lit from within and full of palms, with a rover in the foreground on a rocky red plain under a dusty sky.

The prime and alternate crew of HERA Campaign 7 Mission 4 standing in dark flight suits outside the Human Exploration Research Analog habitat at NASA's Johnson Space Center, holding the mission patch lettered Wilder, Hundley, Magas, Alsuwaidi, Snyder and Wilson, with a UAE flag on the patch and on one crew member's sleeve.

Officials and students applauding beside the newly unveiled dark stone sign of the Korea AeroSpace Administration at Sacheon, the stone carrying the government emblem, the words 대한민국우주항공청 and the inscribed date 2024. 5. 27, photographed at the opening ceremony on 30 May 2024.
